# 1.2.91 - lighter token moves on the mover's browser, the Stained Glass buttons' edges, a stash in every Bedroom, and the first run: Season setup, Pre-season checks and the requirements window

Stages E89 and E20 ship with this version as one release. E89 (line A): token moves ask fewer verdicts again on the mover's
browser and on a `sightRefresh`, the shared cut of the Stained Glass buttons takes the corners and not the border, and a
Bedroom gets its owner's open stash on every usual road, with a migration for the Bedrooms of an existing world. E20 (line B,
merged at 55ed2e36): a GM new to the module is pointed at the first step; the checklist, Pre-season checks and the Doors tab
count rooms and students by the same rules; the reports speak the table's language; a module that did not start leaves Foundry
as it was; what the module changes in Foundry is told and can be given back. 30 commits on 1.2.90 (12ff1b62), up to 1d19c003,
the last before the release commit. What was counted and what was not is in Known gaps and Checked.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **What changes in a running world.** One migration runs, `bedroomStashes` (since 1.2.91, `migrate.mjs`), once, on the
   primary GM's browser, at the first load of 1.2.91: every Bedroom whose owner (an actor of the world) has no stash in it is
   given an open one, and the GMs get one report, "Bedroom stashes given", by scene with each Bedroom's owner. A world where
   every Bedroom has its stash gets no report; on a browser that is not the primary the clause does nothing; a second run,
   forced, finds none and writes nothing. It is a migration and not a sweep at every load, so a stash you removed on purpose
   before 1.2.91 is given back once, and is not given back again after: remove it again on the Stashes tab. The trial hall
   holds no Bedroom. Four settings are new, none of them in a settings window as a dial: `foundryBefore` (world) and
   `foundryBeforeClient` (client) keep the value a Foundry, Daggerheart or module setting had before the module first changed
   it, `foundryGivenBack` (world, true after Give back) and `startHereShown` (client: Where to start was told to this
   browser's GM once). One button is new among the module's own settings in Configure Settings, "Give back Foundry's
   settings" (GMs only). A world that an earlier version already changed has no kept value for those settings: the window says
   so and Give them back sets Daggerheart's defaults (both on). `module.json` rewords the reason of three required modules (Dice
   So Nice, Isometric Perspective, LiveKit AVClient). A scene created after the migration (an import or a copy) with a Bedroom
   whose owner has no stash gives that owner one on the primary GM's browser and tells the GMs. No GM store, no bridge row,
   no socket event, no console call and no keybinding is added (`gm-stores.mjs`, `gm-bridge.mjs`, `api.mjs` have no diff
   from 12ff1b62). `lang/en.json` goes from 4113 strings to 4277 (166 added, 2 removed, 12 reworded) and `lang/pl.json` from
   4930 to 5122 (194 added, 2 removed, 12 reworded), counted with node on both files at 12ff1b62 and at HEAD; the two removed
   in each are `DRPG.Requirements.intro` (now `.one`/`.other`) and `DRPG.Season.roomCountLine`.
3. **The owner's answers.** E89, of 28.10 and 30.10: the lag is on every browser ("U wszystkich chyba"), so the watchers' and
   the GM's path is included; the edges are in Stained Glass, in many places, the GM Panel for one; every road that leaves a
   Bedroom without a stash is fixed ("Napraw kazda"); the Bedrooms of existing worlds get theirs once, reported ("Tak"); the
   old owner keeps their stash in a Bedroom given to someone else ("Tak"). E20, of 29.10 and 30.10: all 24 issues are built;
   Dice So Nice stays required; the overflow threshold gets only a hint; in a running game "{n} students still have actions to
   spend." stays first and an unfinished Season setup row is a second, quieter line; the language of the requirements window,
   the 8 MiB, 8 s and floor readings of the room pictures and the 10% limit of a room-less map stand as built; README keeps
   its requirements table as it was.

## At the table

### For the GM

- **A Bedroom has its stash.** A Bedroom made the usual way gives its owner an open stash: when you mark the room and give
  it to a student in either order, in one Apply or in two, when the console's `setVaultRoom` makes it, and when you press
  Apply on the Stashes tab without touching a cell (a cell you did not change is left as it was, so Apply no longer erases a
  stash it has just made). The tier-2 test found two of these roads, the owner first and the room marked later, and
  `setVaultRoom`, red before. When a Bedroom is given to someone else, the old owner keeps their stash and what is in it and
  the new owner gets their own open stash. A stash you remove on the Stashes tab stays removed.
- **Bedrooms of an existing world:** the report "Bedroom stashes given", once, on the primary GM's browser (Before installing,
  2). It reads: "Each bedroom below had no stash for its owner, so its owner was given an open one. If you had removed one on
  purpose, remove it again on Room Setup's Stashes tab."
- **When the table lags: a token dragged across rooms** (GM handbook, "When the table lags"). Run
  `await game.drpg.fps({ seconds: 5 })` on the mover's browser, on a watcher's and on your own during a drag, and send the
  three results with each browser's theme. What 1.2.91 changed is counted on the module's model of a drag, not at a table;
  the lag is not known to be gone.
- **The edges of the Stained Glass buttons.** The cut shared by the GM Panel's tiles, the footer buttons and the messenger's
  send button no longer covers the last pixel of the border (`stained-glass.css`, `--drpg-clip-out`, 0.5 px while the lit brush
  is off). Read in software Chromium only; if an edge still vanishes or flickers, send which control, the theme, the screen
  size, the page zoom and a screenshot.
- **First run** (GM handbook, "Starting a world"). On a world with no campaign name and no students a GM's first load opens
  "Where to start" once in each GM's browser: "Start here: GM panel > Set the season up. Its list walks you through a season in
  the order it is built, and the GM panel's Next line names the first thing still to do." with a button that opens it.
  **Set the season up** opens at its top with the campaign name in focus, in a block, "This campaign"; a row's Open brings its
  window in front, and a round trip through a row comes back where you were. A row ticks only once it has checked something:
  with no students the rows about students read "Waiting for the cast: create the students first.". Until the required rows
  hold, the GM panel's Next line reads "The season is not set up yet. Next in Set the season up: {step}." and never offers the
  Eclipse; once the season has started (the clock past chapter 1, day 1, session 1, the first time of day - the implementer's
  reading of the owner's words, not confirmed by the owner) "{n} students still have actions to spend." stays first and the
  Season setup row comes under it as a second, quieter line. The Next line judges the rooms on the school whichever scene is on
  screen, and a row the module cannot finish (a self-hosted LiveKit server whose secret is in the world) is drawn crossed and
  skipped.
- **One count of rooms and students.** The Doors tab, the checklist and Pre-season checks count the same way: rooms marked,
  not owned, not "No privacy", locked rooms counted; students the living. The "map has rooms" row needs at most 10% of the
  scene's own area in no room (the padding around the map does not count) and no problem left from the scene's last Check the
  rooms, read floor by floor with the worst floor named; the Doors tab shows a region nobody decided apart and counts it only
  once you change its box.
- **Check the rooms on this scene** says once, above the list, what each kind of finding means, and gives each room a short
  fact and **Show on map**, which pans to the spot and marks it on your screen only, on the finding's floor. With no scene
  on the canvas it says "No scene on the canvas", on a scene with no rooms "No rooms on this scene". It also warns when one
  room's pieces differ in No privacy, owner or height. The rooms row is drawn again as soon as the check ends.
- **Pre-season checks** are in the table's language and name no console command: the cast (the count of students and of the
  living, who lacks the starting resources, with the fix "To fix it: open the sheet and press the wand beside the name."), one
  line a scene with its tick or cross, room pictures only when one needs a word (a picture that does not load, one over 4096
  px on a side or 8 MiB, one whose size the server did not give, one that did not finish loading within 8 s: "These room pictures
  did not finish loading within {s} seconds, ..."), the voice rows only when they hold (A/V off, video only, video nobody
  watches), and the anonymity audit, which asks "fix these" only for a sheet every player owns and offers "Set them to
  Observer"; with Keep character sheets anonymous off it lists the Observer sheets and names the switch.
- **What the module changes in Foundry, and giving it back** (GM handbook, "What the module changes in Foundry, and giving it
  back"). The handbook lists the two Daggerheart automations that Breakdown and Wounded replace, the file-browser permissions, Isometric
  Perspective's welcome window, Daggerheart's welcome journal, LiveKit's voice inside the Foundry window, the camera dock, the
  rooms' take-over of vision, fog and light, and the table's one dice look. "Give back Foundry's settings", in Configure
  Settings, has "Give them back" and "Hold them again"; only a full Gamemaster gives back, each part on its own. The dice look
  does not come back, and nobody's own earlier look is known. Before you switch the module off, press Give them back and turn
  "Rooms decide what players can see" off. When you switch it on again it holds nothing until you press Hold them again: you
  are asked at each start, Set the season up shows a row and Pre-season checks say so.
- **Smaller:** the overflow row reads "Suggested for {students} and {pools}: {x}." (12 plus half the living students, held to
  the range; the default stays 20); the rules manager shows the motive in force with its time left and "Withdraw"; a number
  field's buttons say the step they move by, "One more" and "One fewer" only at a step of 1; the Despair row names a student
  nobody assigned as "{name} (falls back to {pool})".

### For players

- **Your Bedroom has your stash** on every road the GM may have made it by (the GM's list above); the report of existing
  worlds goes to the GMs only.
- **Token moves:** nothing is added or removed in what you see. A move of your own token inside the rooms you already stand in
  asks your browser for your own token's visibility alone, not every token's; a move into another room asks only the tokens
  the room change can touch. Whether it feels lighter at a table is not measured (LIVE-E89-01).
- **A missing required module:** the notice that stays on screen gives each module's reason in the table's language, in plain
  words ("Voice follows the rooms: you hear the people in the room your character is in, and moving to another room changes
  who hears you."), and counts one missing module as one.
- **Stained Glass:** the messenger's send button wears the same cut as the GM Panel's tiles and was read with it (`?msgr=1`):
  steady T22 at 3 of 4 sizes as cut before, 0 at all 4 after, in software Chromium only (LIVE-E89-04).

### For everybody

- **A module that did not start leaves Foundry as it was:** its stylesheets are taken off the page, its settings and holds do
  not run, and the hotbar and the scene navigation stay where Foundry draws them (read in scenario 00-boot, E20-T3, for a GM whose world has a required module off; the players list is named in a code comment and was not read). What it changed before
  stays until it runs again and a GM gives it back; the requirements window says so.
- **Rooms and students are counted by one rule** in the Doors tab, the checklist and Pre-season checks (GM's list above).
- **New counters** for the table's `fps()` and the harness, in `perf-counters.mjs`: `visibility.applyAll.flags`,
  `visibility.applyRooms`, `visibility.sightPass`, `visibility.roomsChanged`, `visibility.forget`, `visibility.myRooms.walk`,
  `visibility.sliding`, `fog.reactToMove` and `movement.whenAtRest`, with their `.tokens`, `.flags`, `.walks` and `.polls`.

## Known gaps

- **E89-04, partial.** On the mover's own move `visibility.applyToToken` went from 138 to 48, not to 3: the 45 are the
  once-a-second sweep (`reassert.sweep.tokens`) landing in the window. `refreshToken.visibility` went from 46 to 1 and
  `applyAll.tokens` from 46 to 0 (counts on the harness's model, not frame times).
- **E89-11, the edges, partial.** Measured only in software Chromium, headless. There the plain, route and destructive tiles
  of the GM Panel read 0 at 7 sizes; the Projects tile still read counts (L21 T2 B10, L56 T12 B5, L5 T3 B1 at three sizes)
  and the GM Panel's Close button still read them (moving T9, T12 at four sizes, as before). Another panel's footer button
  is as before. The same cut at four other places in `stained-glass.css` (`.drpg-choice`, `.drpg-rest-option`,
  `.drpg-frisk-mode`, the checkboxes, `.drpg-step`, `#drpg-hud .drpg-hud-button`) is unchanged. Never drawn by the probe: the
  sheet band, the pause caption, the action pip, the scene controls, the sidebar tabs. Rotation snap, `will-change` on a
  turned block and the hover and press scales were not tried.
- **Stashes.** Import Data onto an existing scene is an update, not a create, and seeds no stash. The first load of 1.2.91 on
  a real v14 world has not run (the clause was run on the harness only). Room Setup's Stashes tab was not read drawn at a
  table. A removed stash the migration gave back is told in the report only.
- **The moves.** The drag onto a refused route and the GM's own drag of a player's token with a preview are not modelled in
  scenario 86. Memos are still dropped on every `sightPass` (22 forgets and 22 walks during a move on a player's browser),
  and the waits for a token at rest are counted, not merged. `createSetting` is read, not run, by the harness. `delta.ownership`
  on a v14 unlinked token is not read on v14. The nine listener mutants of fix FG2 ran combined in one copy.
- **E20.** `UNCOVERED_LIMIT_PCT` = 10 is a choice, not measured on a real map. The Doors tab's "too many rooms" warning counts
  locked rooms. The console's `checkRegions()` records no room check for the checklist. `diagnoseDespair`, the console report,
  is still English. Room Setup's fog tab shows the worst floor's percentage without naming it. Automations go back to
  Daggerheart 2.6.5's defaults (2.10.x not read); scenes get their vision back from turning off "Rooms decide what players can
  see", not from the button. README's requirements table keeps the old Isometric and Dice So Nice wording.
- **LIVE rows, not tried at a table (AUDIT 9.2).** E89: item 343 LIVE-E89-02 (does the drag's preview and `sightRefresh` fire
  each frame on v14), 344 LIVE-E89-03 (how many `updateToken` one dragged path delivers), 345 LIVE-E89-04 (the GM Panel's tile
  edges on an ordinary graphics card), 346 LIVE-E89-01 (`fps({ seconds: 5 })` during a drag on 1.2.90 and on 1.2.91), 347
  LIVE-E89-05 (a Bedroom's stash and the report on the owner's world). E20 (AUDIT 9.2 numbers them B-E20-1 to B-E20-7, with no
  item number): B-E20-1 LIVE-E20-01 (Season setup and Pre-season on screen at 1366x768 and 1920x1080), B-E20-2 LIVE-E20-02 (a
  world without Dice So Nice), B-E20-3 LIVE-E20-03 (from install to the first Eclipse by the windows alone), B-E20-4
  LIVE-E20-04 (room pictures on a real server, three probes at a time), B-E20-5 LIVE-E20-05 (Show on map on a real canvas), B-E20-6
  LIVE-E20-06 (Give back Foundry's settings in a real settings window), B-E20-7 LIVE-E20-07 (the 10% limit on the owner's map).
- **Read in the code, not run.** The restored scroll and focus of a Season setup round trip, and the window's stacking against
  Foundry's own windows, have no layout in the harness; the Next line's school default is read by a source pattern in R1523
  and called by E20-T8.
